- A dual-polarisation short-aperiodic-loaded-loop or SALLA-type antenna mounted on each station.
- Radio emission from geomagnetic and Askaryan processes is not absorbed by the atmosphere.
It gives a calorimetric measure of the electromagnetic energy, roughly ±10–15% resolution.
- Inclined showers have the largest radio footprints, tens of km² at 80–84°.
The 0.7 km grid therefore samples many antennas per event, which suits this zenith band well.
- Radio runs day and night, giving close to 100% duty cycle.

- The radio footprint also constrains the distance to shower maximum, which gives an extra handle on composition.

Underground Muon Detectors (UMDs)

**Technology:** Buried scintillator panels (plastic scintillator, ~30 m² per station, ~2.3 m soil overburden), coupled to silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), co-located with a subset of existing water-Cherenkov stations — following the design proven at the Pierr
- Soil overburden of ~540 g/cm² eliminates the EM component entirely; only muons penetrate
- Provides a **direct, unambiguous muon count** per station, decoupled from the EM signal in the water-Cherenkov detector above
- At 80–84° zenith, the EM shadow means even the surface detectors are muon-dominated, but the UMD gives the absolute muon reference needed to calibrate the surface signal
- The water-Cherenkov station above simultaneously records the residual EM component and the total particle density, enabling genuine component separation
- Achieving 30% muon number resolution at 10^19.5 eV requires individual station muon counts accurate to ~10–15%, which scintillator + SiPM achieves routinely

- **Deployment priority:** stations within ~1500 m of likely shower core positions for the inclined-shower sample; roughly 400–500 stations needed for adequate lateral distribution function sampling at 80–84°
Surface Scintillator Detectors (SSDs) Above Each Water-Cherenkov Station
**Technology:** 3–4 m² plastic scintillator tiles with SiPM readout, mounted on the lid/roof of each existing polyethylene vessel.

- A thin scintillator (radiation length ~40× shorter interaction path than 1.3 m water) responds almost exclusively to **particle number** rather than energy deposit, with a very different muon/EM ratio than the water tank

- The **ratio of SSD signal to WCD signal** at the same station provides, on a station-by-station basis, an estimator of the local muon fraction — this is the AugerPrime "two eyes on the same shower" principle
- For inclined showers specifically, the SSD resolves the residual EM halo near the core from the muon plateau far from the core, improving the lateral distribution function fit
- Thin (5 mm) scintillator adds negligible weight and no structural modification to the closed polyethylene vessel — the lid is designed to support PMT housings already

**Technology:** Single unified FPGA readout board per station (replacing the current separate timing/DAQ boards), with ~120 MHz flash ADC channels for WCD PMTs, SSD SiPMs, and UMD SiPMs; GPS-disciplined 10 ns timing; expanded local memory buffer (≥8 GB flash);
